newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile lifts forex controls for investments abroad.
newsitem.headline: Chile lifts forex controls for investments abroad.

text.p: Chile's Central Bank eliminated restrictions on access to local foreign exchange markets for Chilean companies that want to invest abroad.
In a series of announcements on forex policies, the bank also lifted the reserve requirement known locally as the ''encaje'' on profit remittances and other benefits from Chilean investments abroad.
But the bank made a point of saying that there was no change on rules affecting new capital inflow within Chile -- meaning the ''encaje'' will stay in effect for foreign investments in Chile.

The announcements mainly affected Chilean firms doing business abroad, with little change for foreigners investing here. Big Chilean companies, especially in the electricity and pension fund sectors, have long been hankering for deregulation to allow them to branch out from the small domestic market and go overseas.
''The measures...eliminate restrictions on access to money in the formal foreign exchange market for investment operations abroad,'' said a Central Bank statement.
The Chilean economy and forex markets are now strong enough to justify the lifting of restrictions on capital outflow, said the statement.

''This move is possible because the structural conditions of the economy and its external sector are growing constantly more solid, allowing us to finish lifting restrictions on capital outflow,'' said the statement.

The bank streamlined other rules on Chilean investment abroad, including ''reduction of administrative controls and restrictions affecting investment operations abroad such as previous authorization (and) periodic reporting rules,'' it said.

It also ended the reserve requirement, or ''encaje,'' on profit remittances and benefits from Chilean investment abroad ''as long as the existence of the original investment and the continuity of it until its liquidation are proved.''

But the bank was clear in setting no change in the ''encaje'' on foreign companies investing in Chile, a rule which foreign investors consider onerous as it keeps a large percentage of their investment bottled up in the Central Bank.

''The Council of the Central Bank also decided it was in the interests (of the country) to maintain restrictions on capital inflow with the goal of continuing policies that preserve the stability of the (peso) currency and which maintain adequate levels and structures in foreign financing,'' said the statement.
